descriptors.description: Eval coverage lets you compare authored AI behavior against known cases and catch regressions before prompts, agents, flows, or pipelines drift.

fixes.description: Add an Eval that covers this definition so regressions can be detected.
fixes.title: Add eval coverage

descriptors.impact: Uncovered definitions can regress silently when prompts, models, tools, or orchestration logic changes.
descriptors.rationale: Eval coverage lets you compare authored AI behavior against known cases and catch regressions before prompts, agents, flows, or pipelines drift.
descriptors.title: Definition has no eval coverage

descriptors.description: Index-visible handoff targets let you inspect the handoff path, connect parent and delegated work, and trust the trace tree when agents transfer control.

fixes.description: Define and export the target agent with a stable id, or update the handoff id so it points at a index-visible agent.
fixes.title: Make the handoff target visible

descriptors.impact: A handoff to an unindexed or missing agent can appear as an orphaned tool call, missing branch, or disconnected trace segment.
descriptors.rationale: Index-visible handoff targets let you inspect the handoff path, connect parent and delegated work, and trust the trace tree when agents transfer control.
descriptors.title: Agent handoff target is not index-visible

descriptors.description: Prompt input schemas are the TypeScript contract for prompt inputs, context joins, replay, eval cases, and devtools inspection.

fixes.description: Add an input schema to the prompt so calls, eval cases, and traces share one inspectable contract.
fixes.title: Declare prompt input

descriptors.impact: Untyped prompt inputs are harder to validate, replay, compare, and safely refactor as the prompt evolves.
descriptors.rationale: Prompt input schemas are the TypeScript contract for prompt inputs, context joins, replay, eval cases, and devtools inspection.
descriptors.title: Prompt has no input schema

descriptors.description: Prompt output schemas make generated objects inspectable and comparable, and let evals assert structured behavior instead of only text.

fixes.description: Add an output schema when this prompt is expected to produce structured data or feed downstream logic.
fixes.title: Declare prompt output

descriptors.impact: Unstructured prompt outputs can make downstream code, replay, and regression checks depend on ad hoc parsing.
descriptors.rationale: Prompt output schemas make generated objects inspectable and comparable, and let evals assert structured behavior instead of only text.
descriptors.title: Prompt has no output schema

descriptors.description: Injected contexts and injectables can make a prompt require fields that are not visible in the prompt authored input schema. Surfacing those fields keeps prompt calls, eval cases, and replay inputs honest.

fixes.description: Either add the field to the prompt input schema, make the injected source optional, or document why the injected requirement is intentionally hidden.
fixes.title: Make the requirement visible

descriptors.impact: Callers can miss a required field because the requirement is hidden behind prompt composition instead of declared on the prompt itself.
descriptors.rationale: Injected contexts and injectables can make a prompt require fields that are not visible in the prompt authored input schema. Surfacing those fields keeps prompt calls, eval cases, and replay inputs honest.
descriptors.title: Prompt has injected required input

descriptors.description: When multiple injected sources contribute the same input field with obviously incompatible schemas, callers and eval cases cannot know which contract is authoritative.

fixes.description: Rename one field, make the schemas compatible, or move the shared field into the prompt input schema so every injected source agrees on the contract.
fixes.title: Align contributed schemas

descriptors.impact: Prompt calls can validate differently depending on composition order, and generated devtools or replay forms may show a misleading contract.
descriptors.rationale: When multiple injected sources contribute the same input field with obviously incompatible schemas, callers and eval cases cannot know which contract is authoritative.
descriptors.title: Prompt has conflicting injected input

descriptors.description: A field required by an injected source becomes only conditionally required when the source is guarded by when, match, or runtime-dependent composition. The global prompt schema must keep it optional, but authors still need to know which branch needs it.

fixes.description: Keep the global field optional, but document or model the branch where it is required. If the branch always runs, remove the conditional wrapper.
fixes.title: Document the branch requirement

descriptors.impact: Eval cases and callers can miss branch-specific input unless the conditional requirement is visible in the Project Index.
descriptors.rationale: A field required by an injected source becomes only conditionally required when the source is guarded by when, match, or runtime-dependent composition. The global prompt schema must keep it optional, but authors still need to know which branch needs it.
descriptors.title: Prompt has conditionally required input

descriptors.description: Context input schemas make conditional and dynamic context injection explicit, inspectable, and type-safe across prompt composition.

fixes.description: Use an inline or import-safe schema for the context input so Crux can project the contract into the index.
fixes.title: Declare resolvable context input

descriptors.impact: Dynamic context without a resolved input contract can hide missing fields until runtime and make context windows harder to debug.
descriptors.rationale: Context input schemas make conditional and dynamic context injection explicit, inspectable, and type-safe across prompt composition.
descriptors.title: Dynamic context has no resolved input schema

descriptors.description: Runtime-dependent injection is allowed, but the Project Index cannot fully explain the prompt or context graph from source alone. Marking the dynamic edge makes that blind spot visible.

fixes.description: Move stable dependencies into a static use array or keep the dynamic path intentional and documented with a suppression reason.
fixes.title: Declare static use when possible

descriptors.impact: Devtools, eval coverage, and static linting may under-report the contexts, memory, or injectables that can affect this definition.
descriptors.rationale: Runtime-dependent injection is allowed, but the Project Index cannot fully explain the prompt or context graph from source alone. Marking the dynamic edge makes that blind spot visible.
descriptors.title: Injection dependency is runtime-dependent

descriptors.description: Contexts and injectables can contribute tools dynamically. That keeps authoring flexible, but it means the model-facing tool surface cannot be fully inspected from static source.

fixes.description: Prefer static tool maps or named tool contributors where possible. Suppress only when the runtime-selected tool set is intentional.
fixes.title: Expose stable tool names

descriptors.impact: A prompt or context may gain tools that are absent from the static Project Index, making safety review, replay, and eval setup less precise.
descriptors.rationale: Contexts and injectables can contribute tools dynamically. That keeps authoring flexible, but it means the model-facing tool surface cannot be fully inspected from static source.
descriptors.title: Injected tools are runtime-dependent

descriptors.description: Tools can enter a prompt through contexts and injectables rather than the prompt body itself. Surfacing that indirect tool surface makes safety review, eval setup, and replay easier to reason about.

fixes.description: Keep the indirect tool surface intentional, document the injected source, or move stable tools closer to the prompt when direct visibility matters.
fixes.title: Review the indirect tool source

descriptors.impact: Authors can miss model-facing tools because the prompt does not declare them directly, especially when the tool source is multiple injection hops away.
descriptors.rationale: Tools can enter a prompt through contexts and injectables rather than the prompt body itself. Surfacing that indirect tool surface makes safety review, eval setup, and replay easier to reason about.
descriptors.title: Prompt receives tools through injection

descriptors.description: An index-visible injectable that is never reached from any prompt, context, or injectable may be dead authoring surface or a dynamically consumed dependency the static graph cannot see.

fixes.description: Wire the injectable into a static use path, remove it if it is stale, or suppress the finding when it is intentionally consumed dynamically or externally.
fixes.title: Use, remove, or suppress

descriptors.impact: Unused injectables can make prompt composition harder to scan and can hide stale schema or tool contracts.
descriptors.rationale: An index-visible injectable that is never reached from any prompt, context, or injectable may be dead authoring surface or a dynamically consumed dependency the static graph cannot see.
descriptors.title: Injectable is not used by the indexed graph

descriptors.description: A context that is not reachable from any prompt, context, or injectable may be dead authoring surface or may only be selected through dynamic runtime composition.

fixes.description: Wire the context into a static use path, remove it if it is stale, or suppress the finding when dynamic or external composition is intentional.
fixes.title: Use, remove, or suppress

descriptors.impact: Unused contexts can keep stale prompt text, schema requirements, or tool surfaces alive without clear consumers.
descriptors.rationale: A context that is not reachable from any prompt, context, or injectable may be dead authoring surface or may only be selected through dynamic runtime composition.
descriptors.title: Context is not used by the indexed graph

descriptors.description: A static-looking use entry that cannot be resolved to an index-visible definition makes the injection graph incomplete and can hide schema, tools, memory, or prompt text.

fixes.description: Export or inline the target definition, avoid opaque aliases for static use entries, or intentionally mark the dependency as dynamic.
fixes.title: Make the target resolvable

descriptors.impact: Devtools and lints may under-report what affects the prompt or context because a visible use target could not be linked.
descriptors.rationale: A static-looking use entry that cannot be resolved to an index-visible definition makes the injection graph incomplete and can hide schema, tools, memory, or prompt text.
descriptors.title: Injection target is unresolved

descriptors.description: Deeply injected schema requirements are harder to discover from the prompt surface and harder to keep aligned with callers and eval cases.

fixes.description: Move important input requirements closer to the prompt, reduce composition depth, or document why the deep injection path is intentional.
fixes.title: Flatten or document the chain

descriptors.impact: A prompt can appear simple while relying on fields contributed several composition hops away, making refactors and replay setup more fragile.
descriptors.rationale: Deeply injected schema requirements are harder to discover from the prompt surface and harder to keep aligned with callers and eval cases.
descriptors.title: Injected input comes from a deep chain

descriptors.description: Flow argument schemas document the durable or immediate entry contract and make flow starts, resumes, and eval cases inspectable.

fixes.description: Add an import-safe args schema or Convex validator object so Crux can project the flow input contract.
fixes.title: Declare flow args

descriptors.impact: Untyped flow arguments can make resumed work and flow evals depend on undocumented input shapes.
descriptors.rationale: Flow argument schemas document the durable or immediate entry contract and make flow starts, resumes, and eval cases inspectable.
descriptors.title: Flow args are not inspectable

descriptors.description: Tool input schemas make model-emitted arguments inspectable, validateable, and easier for your team to debug across traces, evals, and generated devtools UI.

fixes.description: Add a Zod or JSON-schema-compatible input schema to the tool parameters so arguments are validated and inspectable.
fixes.title: Declare tool parameters

descriptors.impact: Untyped tool calls are harder to validate, inspect, replay, and explain when an agent makes a bad call.
descriptors.rationale: Tool input schemas make model-emitted arguments inspectable, validateable, and easier for your team to debug across traces, evals, and generated devtools UI.
descriptors.title: Tool has no input schema

descriptors.description: A model-output adapter makes tool results explicit for traces, replay, and debugging the model intent-to-execution chain.

fixes.description: Add a toModelOutput adapter when the tool result needs a stable, inspectable model-facing representation.
fixes.title: Declare model output mapping

descriptors.impact: Raw tool outputs can be hard to inspect or compare when the application result differs from what the model receives.
descriptors.rationale: A model-output adapter makes tool results explicit for traces, replay, and debugging the model intent-to-execution chain.
descriptors.title: Tool output is not model-inspectable

descriptors.description: Suspension paths cross time, approval, and runtime boundaries, so you need regression coverage for resume behavior and stale pending work.

fixes.description: Add a flow eval that exercises the suspend/resume path, including the expected approval or signal.
fixes.title: Cover suspend and resume

descriptors.impact: A broken suspend/resume path can strand user work or continue with stale state after approval.
descriptors.rationale: Suspension paths cross time, approval, and runtime boundaries, so you need regression coverage for resume behavior and stale pending work.
descriptors.title: Suspending flow has no eval coverage

descriptors.description: Flow step labels are durable replay identities. Repeating a label in one flow body makes cached output ambiguous across retries, suspension, and resume.

fixes.description: Give each flow.step() call a distinct literal label, and encode loop iteration or branch meaning in the label only when it is stable across resumes.
fixes.title: Use unique step labels

descriptors.impact: A repeated step label can return the wrong cached output or fail at runtime before the flow reaches later work.
descriptors.rationale: Flow step labels are durable replay identities. Repeating a label in one flow body makes cached output ambiguous across retries, suspension, and resume.
descriptors.title: Flow repeats a step label

descriptors.description: Flow signal delivery is keyed by signal name and consumed after one delivery. Repeating a suspend name in one flow body makes later resumes depend on source-order replay rather than a distinct signal contract.

fixes.description: Give each suspend point a distinct literal name, or split repeated waits into separate flows until scoped/repeating signal attempts are supported.
fixes.title: Use unique suspend names

descriptors.impact: A repeated suspend name can make approvals ambiguous and can strand a later wait behind an already-used signal name.
descriptors.rationale: Flow signal delivery is keyed by signal name and consumed after one delivery. Repeating a suspend name in one flow body makes later resumes depend on source-order replay rather than a distinct signal contract.
descriptors.title: Flow repeats a suspend name

descriptors.description: A local signal map is the public signal contract for a flow. Literal suspend names outside that map cannot be signaled through the typed handle and usually mean the runtime contract drifted from the authored type contract.

fixes.description: Add the suspend name to the flow signals map, or rename the suspend call to one of the declared signal keys.
fixes.title: Declare or rename the signal

descriptors.impact: A flow may suspend at a signal that callers cannot discover or type-check through the flow handle.
descriptors.rationale: A local signal map is the public signal contract for a flow. Literal suspend names outside that map cannot be signaled through the typed handle and usually mean the runtime contract drifted from the authored type contract.
descriptors.title: Flow suspends on an undeclared signal

descriptors.description: Writable workspaces can mutate drafts, files, and artifacts; guardrails help you keep those mutations policy-checked, auditable, and observable.

fixes.description: Attach a guardrail to the workspace or its write/delete tools so mutations are inspectable and policy-checked.
fixes.title: Attach a guardrail

descriptors.impact: Unprotected workspace writes can damage user content or make file mutations difficult to audit after the fact.
descriptors.rationale: Writable workspaces can mutate drafts, files, and artifacts; guardrails help you keep those mutations policy-checked, auditable, and observable.
descriptors.title: Writable workspace has no guardrail

descriptors.description: Distinct effect() call sites declare the same literal id and version.

fixes.description: Change the id or version, or re-export the existing Effect definition instead of calling effect() again.
fixes.title: Make the Effect identity unique

descriptors.impact: Runtime registration rejects conflicting definitions and Catalog/runtime joins become ambiguous.
descriptors.rationale: Effect receipt and recovery identity is the (id, version) pair and must resolve to one definition.
descriptors.title: Effect identity is defined more than once

descriptors.description: Safety policy ids are used in decisions, traces, Project Index rows, and test matchers. Reusing an id makes it hard to tell which policy blocked, rewrote, or retried a turn.

fixes.description: Give each guardrail, constraint, and tool policy a unique id within the project safety surface.
fixes.title: Rename one policy

descriptors.impact: Duplicate policy ids can make Devtools, observability, and Eval assertions point at the wrong safety policy.
descriptors.rationale: Safety policy ids are used in decisions, traces, Project Index rows, and test matchers. Reusing an id makes it hard to tell which policy blocked, rewrote, or retried a turn.
descriptors.title: Safety policy id is duplicated

descriptors.description: A prompt or agent can bind one canonical Thread history. Resolving multiple Thread targets makes the history source and accepted-turn commit destination ambiguous.

fixes.description: Remove the extra Thread entry from the prompt or agent use graph so managed execution resolves exactly one canonical history.
fixes.title: Keep one Thread binding

descriptors.impact: Conflicting Thread bindings can make managed execution read from or publish accepted turns to an unintended conversation tree.
descriptors.rationale: A prompt or agent can bind one canonical Thread history. Resolving multiple Thread targets makes the history source and accepted-turn commit destination ambiguous.
descriptors.title: Definition resolves multiple Thread bindings

descriptors.description: Active Thread ids identify one canonical conversation tree. Reusing an id in multiple active definitions makes storage, runtime evidence, and developer tooling point at an ambiguous Thread.

fixes.description: Rename one thread() id or remove the duplicate active export so each canonical conversation tree has one authored identity.
fixes.title: Give each active Thread a unique id

descriptors.impact: Duplicate active Thread ids can make unrelated definitions share canonical history or attach tooling to the wrong authored source.
descriptors.rationale: Active Thread ids identify one canonical conversation tree. Reusing an id in multiple active definitions makes storage, runtime evidence, and developer tooling point at an ambiguous Thread.
descriptors.title: Thread id is active more than once

descriptors.description: Long-lived episodic and semantic memory can accumulate stale or sensitive facts; a retention policy makes lifetime and cleanup behavior explicit.

fixes.description: Add an eviction or retention policy to long-lived memory so cleanup behavior is inspectable.
fixes.title: Declare memory retention

descriptors.impact: Memory without a visible retention policy can silently grow, preserve stale context, or keep user data longer than intended.
descriptors.rationale: Long-lived episodic and semantic memory can accumulate stale or sensitive facts; a retention policy makes lifetime and cleanup behavior explicit.
descriptors.title: Long-lived memory has no retention policy

descriptors.description: A memory, blackboard, or workspace that receives writes but has no visible read path can indicate unreachable context, forgotten state, or an output-only side effect that should be intentional.

fixes.description: Add a index-visible read path for this resource, or suppress the rule with a reason when the write is intentionally output-only.
fixes.title: Connect or document the read path

descriptors.impact: Written-but-unread state can make agents appear to remember or persist work that is never actually used by prompts, tools, flows, or later runs.
descriptors.rationale: A memory, blackboard, or workspace that receives writes but has no visible read path can indicate unreachable context, forgotten state, or an output-only side effect that should be intentional.
descriptors.title: State resource is written but never read

descriptors.description: Consensus compositions need an inspectable decision policy so users can understand why one answer, plan, or agent output won.

fixes.description: Add a index-visible judge agent or scorer to the consensus composition so the decision policy is inspectable.
fixes.title: Attach a judge or scorer

descriptors.impact: Without a visible judge or scorer, consensus behavior can look arbitrary in traces and may be hard to test or tune.
descriptors.rationale: Consensus compositions need an inspectable decision policy so users can understand why one answer, plan, or agent output won.
descriptors.title: Consensus has no visible judge or scorer

descriptors.description: Shared blackboards can receive writes from multiple agents; a conflict policy helps your team understand and debug merge behavior.

fixes.description: Declare a blackboard conflict policy, such as consensus, judge, or last-writer-wins, when multiple agents can write shared state.
fixes.title: Declare a conflict policy

descriptors.impact: Concurrent agent writes can overwrite or contradict each other without an explicit policy for resolving shared state.
descriptors.rationale: Shared blackboards can receive writes from multiple agents; a conflict policy helps your team understand and debug merge behavior.
descriptors.title: Shared blackboard has no conflict policy

descriptors.description: Stable routing ids let index definitions, route decision spans, and Eval history join reliably even when variables or files are renamed.

fixes.description: Add id to router(), split(), retry(), cascade(), or fallback() options so authored routing and runtime spans share a stable join key.
fixes.title: Add a routing id

descriptors.impact: Routes can still be indexed from variable names, but runtime joins and historical comparisons are less durable across refactors.
descriptors.rationale: Stable routing ids let index definitions, route decision spans, and Eval history join reliably even when variables or files are renamed.
descriptors.title: Routing primitive has no stable id

descriptors.description: Routers need an explicit default route so unknown classifier outputs remain observable and deterministic instead of failing or silently depending on adapter behavior.

fixes.description: Add a default entry to the router routes map and point it at the safest fallback model or policy.
fixes.title: Add default route

descriptors.impact: A classifier returning an unexpected key can produce confusing route decisions and incomplete route coverage in traces.
descriptors.rationale: Routers need an explicit default route so unknown classifier outputs remain observable and deterministic instead of failing or silently depending on adapter behavior.
descriptors.title: Router has no default route

descriptors.description: Route, split route, retry target, tier, and fallback option targets should connect to index-visible agents, prompts, or nested routing primitives so users can inspect the authored decision graph.

fixes.description: Reference an exported Crux definition or routing primitive, or keep raw model targets intentional and suppress this rule with a reason.
fixes.title: Make target visible

descriptors.impact: Unresolved route targets appear as plain model references, which limits architecture views, impact analysis, and runtime span joins.
descriptors.rationale: Route, split route, retry target, tier, and fallback option targets should connect to index-visible agents, prompts, or nested routing primitives so users can inspect the authored decision graph.
descriptors.title: Routing target is not index-visible

descriptors.description: A cascade tier without an evaluator accepts by default, so any following tiers are never reached unless that tier throws.

fixes.description: Add evaluate to non-terminal tiers, or move unconditional accept tiers to the end of the cascade.
fixes.title: Add evaluator or reorder tiers

descriptors.impact: Expensive backup tiers may look configured but never run, making quality escalation and cost expectations misleading.
descriptors.rationale: A cascade tier without an evaluator accepts by default, so any following tiers are never reached unless that tier throws.
descriptors.title: Cascade tier makes later tiers unreachable

descriptors.description: Recipe steps are only explainable in devtools when retriever, scorer, and reranker targets resolve to indexed definitions.

fixes.description: Reference an indexed retriever, scorer, or reranker definition from the recipe step, or suppress this rule if the dependency is intentionally external.
fixes.title: Export or define the step target

descriptors.impact: The recipe may still run, but the Project Index cannot show or validate the step dependency that authored code appears to reference.
descriptors.rationale: Recipe steps are only explainable in devtools when retriever, scorer, and reranker targets resolve to indexed definitions.
descriptors.title: RAG recipe step target is unresolved
Relation expansion selects an unknown type
descriptors.description: expandRelations({ types }) should name relation types declared by the Connected Knowledge relation vocabulary visible to the recipe.
descriptors.rationale: expandRelations({ types }) should name relation types declared by the Connected Knowledge relation vocabulary visible to the recipe.
descriptors.impact: Unknown relation selections make graph expansion narrower than authored code suggests and can hide missing connected-knowledge coverage.

fixes.title: Use a declared relation type
fixes.description: Rename the selected type or add it to the relation vocabulary in the knowledge pipeline.

descriptors.title: Knowledge recipe has multiple producer steps
descriptors.description: Connected Knowledge recipes must choose exactly one producer step, either retrieve() or globalSearch().
descriptors.rationale: Connected Knowledge recipes must choose exactly one producer step, either retrieve() or globalSearch().
descriptors.impact: Multiple producers make recipe execution ambiguous and mirror a runtime failure before retrieval can produce hits.

fixes.title: Keep one producer step
fixes.description: Remove the duplicate retrieve() or globalSearch() step so the recipe has exactly one producer.

descriptors.title: Assertion selection names an unknown type
descriptors.description: knowledgeBase().assertions(stage, { types }) and view.assertions(stage, { types }) should select assertion types declared by the stage.
descriptors.rationale: knowledgeBase().assertions(stage, { types }) and view.assertions(stage, { types }) should select assertion types declared by the stage.
descriptors.impact: Unknown assertion selections produce empty or incomplete assertion context even though authored code appears to request a typed subset.

fixes.title: Use a declared assertion type
fixes.description: Rename the selected assertion type or add it to the assertion stage types map.

descriptors.description: Durable runtime target names are persisted as routing identities. Each flow or durable task name must resolve to exactly one target so resumed work wakes the intended code.

fixes.description: Give each flow() or durableTask() declaration a distinct literal name, then run crux runtime generate.
fixes.title: Rename one runtime target

descriptors.impact: Duplicate target names make generated runtime artifacts ambiguous and can block or misroute pending durable work.
descriptors.rationale: Durable runtime target names are persisted as routing identities. Each flow or durable task name must resolve to exactly one target so resumed work wakes the intended code.
descriptors.title: Runtime target name is duplicated

descriptors.description: Runtime artifacts need a durable target name that can be discovered before deployment. Dynamic names cannot be matched to pending work in a fresh process.

fixes.description: Change flow(name, ...) or durableTask(name, ...) to a literal string name and regenerate runtime artifacts.
fixes.title: Use a literal durable name

descriptors.impact: Generated manifests cannot safely include the target, so future wakes may fail with TARGET_NOT_FOUND.
descriptors.rationale: Runtime artifacts need a durable target name that can be discovered before deployment. Dynamic names cannot be matched to pending work in a fresh process.
descriptors.title: Runtime target name is not literal

descriptors.description: Serverless and host-bound runtime entries import targets by named export. Local or nested targets cannot be woken in a later process.

fixes.description: Move the target to a top-level exported const/function declaration, then run crux runtime generate.
fixes.title: Export the target declaration

descriptors.impact: The target is visible to local analysis but cannot be wired into generated runtime entry files.
descriptors.rationale: Serverless and host-bound runtime entries import targets by named export. Local or nested targets cannot be woken in a later process.
descriptors.title: Runtime target is not exported

descriptors.description: Durable background work must name a durable task target so Crux can import and wake it in a later process. Inline closures are request-scoped code, not durable targets.

fixes.description: Move the closure into an exported durableTask() from @use-crux/core/runtime, or use request-scoped defer(callback) when RFC #135 lands.
fixes.title: Use a named durable task

descriptors.impact: The deferred work cannot be represented in generated runtime artifacts or resumed after process exit.
descriptors.rationale: Durable background work must name a durable task target so Crux can import and wake it in a later process. Inline closures are request-scoped code, not durable targets.
descriptors.title: Durable defer target is an inline closure

descriptors.description: Public defer() is invocation-scoped and cannot be replayed safely inside a flow body or step.

fixes.description: Schedule replay-safe durable work through flow.defer().
fixes.title: Use flow.defer

descriptors.impact: Replayed execution can duplicate background work.
descriptors.rationale: A replay could schedule the same request-scoped or durable work more than once.
descriptors.title: Public defer used in replayable code

descriptors.description: Named defer() must be awaited, returned, or included in recognized promise composition.

fixes.description: Await or return the named defer() promise.
fixes.title: Await the promise

descriptors.impact: The host may commit before durable scheduling has succeeded.
descriptors.rationale: The promise is the durable commit barrier for the scheduled intent.
descriptors.title: Named defer promise is not consumed

descriptors.description: Name-bound, time-bound, event-bound, and background APIs need a configured Runtime Engine. Without one, only object-bound flow APIs can keep working.

fixes.description: Add a runtime entry to crux.config.ts, for example runtime: node() for local development.
fixes.title: Configure a runtime

descriptors.impact: The API will throw RUNTIME_REQUIRED when it executes in a project without runtime configuration.
descriptors.rationale: Name-bound, time-bound, event-bound, and background APIs need a configured Runtime Engine. Without one, only object-bound flow APIs can keep working.
descriptors.title: Runtime-bound API used without runtime config

descriptors.description: Flow bodies can replay after suspension. Calls like Date.now() and Math.random() outside flow.step() can produce different replay fingerprints or decisions.

fixes.description: Wrap nondeterministic reads in flow.step() so the first value is cached and replay can reuse it.
fixes.title: Move nondeterminism into a step

descriptors.impact: A resumed flow may diverge from its original execution or block with REPLAY_DIVERGED.
descriptors.rationale: Flow bodies can replay after suspension. Calls like Date.now() and Math.random() outside flow.step() can produce different replay fingerprints or decisions.
descriptors.title: Flow body contains nondeterministic code

descriptors.description: Durable runtime boundaries persist payloads as JSON so they can be replayed, inspected, and delivered across adapters.

fixes.description: Replace the payload with plain JSON data, or store complex data elsewhere and pass a reference.
fixes.title: Pass JSON data

descriptors.impact: Functions, Maps, Sets, class instances, and other non-JSON values fail at runtime with PAYLOAD_NOT_JSON.
descriptors.rationale: Durable runtime boundaries persist payloads as JSON so they can be replayed, inspected, and delivered across adapters.
descriptors.title: Durable runtime payload is not JSON-serializable

descriptors.description: Resolved adapter and model capability evidence proves that the authored media operation, modality, or option is unsupported.

fixes.description: Use an adapter/model that supports the authored operation and modalities, or remove the unsupported option.
fixes.title: Choose a supported capability

descriptors.impact: The authored model operation will fail before producing a usable media result.
descriptors.rationale: Conclusive capability mismatches should fail during review instead of at provider I/O.
descriptors.title: Media capability is unsupported

descriptors.description: Resolved source evidence identifies a provider-file asset passed to a different provider adapter.

fixes.description: Hydrate the asset and upload it through the destination provider before invoking the media operation.
fixes.title: Hydrate or upload the file

descriptors.impact: The destination provider cannot read the file and the model call will fail.
descriptors.rationale: Provider file identifiers are scoped to the provider that created them.
descriptors.title: Provider file belongs to another adapter

descriptors.description: Resolved source evidence proves an opaque AssetRef is passed directly to a model operation.

fixes.description: Call the owning AssetStore get operation and pass the resulting Asset to the model.
fixes.title: Hydrate the asset

descriptors.impact: The model cannot consume the reference and the operation will fail before provider I/O.
descriptors.rationale: AssetRef is a persistence reference, not model-readable media.
descriptors.title: AssetRef is not hydrated

descriptors.description: Indexed media ingest evidence has no required describe or transcribe derivation binding.

fixes.description: Attach an explicit describe or transcribe operation to the media ingest source.
fixes.title: Bind a derivation

descriptors.impact: The ingested media may be stored without searchable semantic content.
descriptors.rationale: Retrieval requires derived text for media that is not directly searchable.
descriptors.title: Media ingest has no text derivation

descriptors.description: Available page or time attribution is not preserved on derived searchable text.

fixes.description: Carry available page or time attribution from the ingest derivation into indexed text records.
fixes.title: Preserve attribution

descriptors.impact: Retrieved evidence cannot be traced back to its page or time range.
descriptors.rationale: Attribution connects retrieved text to the source frame that supports it.
descriptors.title: Derived media text loses attribution

descriptors.description: A proven media output is bound while canonical content and messages are unread in the compiler-visible module graph.

fixes.description: Read content or messages, or explicitly persist the generated Asset with an AssetStore.
fixes.title: Consume the result

descriptors.impact: The operation spends provider time and cost but its media result is lost.
descriptors.rationale: Generated media is useful only when the canonical result is consumed or persisted explicitly.
descriptors.title: Media output is discarded

descriptors.description: Resolved architecture evidence proves raw media is explicitly routed to observability or vector metadata.

fixes.description: Remove raw media from retained metadata and project only bounded modality, size, and MIME facts.
fixes.title: Store a safe descriptor

descriptors.impact: Raw media or bearer references may leak into durable telemetry or retrieval metadata.
descriptors.rationale: Ordinary observability and vector metadata must retain bounded descriptors rather than media payloads.
descriptors.title: Raw media is routed to retained metadata

descriptors.description: A canonical evidence.record call uses a literal kind outside the bounded evidence-kind contract.

fixes.description: Use a bounded custom.* kind for inline data or a canonical kind for an existing artifact reference.
fixes.title: Use a valid evidence kind

descriptors.impact: Runtime evidence authoring rejects this call before collector mutation.
descriptors.rationale: Inline application evidence requires a valid custom.* kind; references may use canonical or custom kinds.
descriptors.title: Evidence kind is invalid

descriptors.description: A canonical evidence.record call uses a reserved canonical artifact kind for inline evidence.

fixes.description: Rename the inline evidence kind to a bounded custom.* value.
fixes.title: Use a custom kind

descriptors.impact: Runtime evidence authoring rejects this call before collector mutation.
descriptors.rationale: Canonical artifact kinds describe Crux-owned sources; inline application evidence must use custom.*.
descriptors.title: Canonical evidence kind is reserved

descriptors.description: Resolved embedding and consumer-call evidence proves that media input uses a modality the dense embedding does not declare.

fixes.description: Use an embedding that declares the authored modality, or pass text input instead.
fixes.title: Choose a compatible embedding

descriptors.impact: The embedding, indexing, knowledge-base, or retrieval call will fail before producing a usable vector.
descriptors.rationale: A text-only or narrower embedding cannot produce comparable vectors for unsupported media.
descriptors.title: Embedding does not support the authored modality

descriptors.description: Resolved consumers share a namespace and vector storage but use different exact dense or sparse embedding identities.

fixes.description: Use matching dense and sparse embedding identities for the namespace, or choose a distinct namespace.
fixes.title: Align the namespace embedding

descriptors.impact: Indexing or retrieval will reject the mixed space, or an existing mixed store will fail loudly at search time.
descriptors.rationale: Similarity search is meaningful only when every vector in a namespace belongs to one embedding space.
descriptors.title: Namespace uses incompatible embedding identities

descriptors.description: Resolved source evidence proves that media is declared, embedded, queried, or indexed through a sparse-only branch.

fixes.description: Route media through a compatible dense embedding and reserve sparse embeddings for text.
fixes.title: Use a dense media embedding

descriptors.impact: The media input cannot produce a sparse vector and sparse-only indexed media is unreachable.
descriptors.rationale: Sparse embeddings are text-only and cannot make media chunks searchable.
descriptors.title: Sparse embedding is combined with media

descriptors.description: A prompt may declare one canonical history projection through history() or history.recent().

fixes.description: Remove all but one history() or history.recent() entry from the prompt use array.
fixes.title: Keep one history projection

descriptors.impact: Multiple projections make history ownership and request planning ambiguous.
descriptors.rationale: One projection must own causal grouping and model-facing history selection.
descriptors.title: Prompt declares multiple history projections

descriptors.description: Representation ladders must follow prefer, summarizable, offloadable, then outermost droppable order.

fixes.description: Use each non-terminal wrapper at most once and make droppable the outermost wrapper.
fixes.title: Reorder the representation ladder

descriptors.impact: Invalid topology can weaken capability ownership or fail request composition before dispatch.
descriptors.rationale: A monotonic wrapper order gives every contributor one unambiguous degradation path.
descriptors.title: Representation wrappers are ordered incorrectly
